correctness.rationale: For fixed target and nonzero k, the second equation forces φ=νx−Φ/k₂, with ν>0. Division by kx on x>0 gives a cosine equal to g(x)=(X−k₀)/(kx)−xe^(r−x)/k, with g=O(x⁻¹) and g′=O(x⁻²). Opposite endpoint cosine values give a root in each high flux cell since |g|<1/2. All roots there lie in the same middle interval, on which the absolute cosine derivative is at least πν√3/2 and has fixed sign, so that the difference is strictly monotone and its root simple. The undivided scalar equation extends analytically past both excluded lower boundaries of x; it is not identically zero because the cosine term has amplitude |k|x along the high integer-flux endpoints. Thus compact portions have only finitely many zeros, including for X=k₀. The Jacobian is −k₂ times the reduced derivative, with the latter equal to kx times the cosine-minus-g derivative at a root. High roots are therefore regular. Counting completed flux cells gives νR+O(1). At center z_j the midpoint sine expansion has sign (−1)^(j+1); the root displacement is O(1/z_j), so replacing 1/x_j by 1/z_j and linearizing the sine incurs O(z_j⁻³), with exponential terms negligible. This even strengthens the stated O(z_j⁻²). For k=0 the x-only first coordinate is strictly increasing to x=2 and strictly decreasing afterwards, with the stated first-coordinate range; the flux equation adds no multiplicity. The claimed proper strip is not a claim of properness as a map into the plane. No bound here is uniform as k goes to zero or asserts forward-invariance of the quadrant.

value.rationale: This is a global inverse-geometry statement for an established model, not an attractor claim or a numerical preimage table. Even arbitrarily weak cosine coupling changes finite inverse valence and a bounded first-coordinate range into surjectivity with one regular branch per high flux cell for every target. The exact slope and location term quantify backward branching and show why conclusions based on bounded input simulations need not transfer to the untruncated system. The exact domain and fixed-parameter scope are essential to that value.
